title: Internal: Hosted Canary Rollouts (GA) Readiness Sync
summary: Cross-team GA readiness check for Hosted canary rollout workflow. Reviewed open blockers (policy propagation staleness, telemetry cardinality, audit log payload/PII, streaming retry pinning edge cases), test status (E2E staging suite + failure injection), and release checklist (feature flag gates, SLOs/alerts, runbook, docs). Confirmed staged GA plan by region and agreed on go/no-go criteria and rollback triggers.
topics: Go/No-Go criteria and staged rollout plan
Routing stickiness and streaming session semantics
Audit logging events and PII review
QA status: E2E tests and regression coverage
questions: Do we require stickiness (request-hash) by default for GA, or keep it optional with a warning?
What’s the default guardrail set for allowing >50% candidate traffic (latency/error/cost deltas)?
What’s the maximum acceptable propagation staleness between regions before we auto-pause rollouts?
next_steps: Finalize GA flag flip plan and region sequence; circulate for sign-off (SRE + Security + Product).
Land telemetry tag allowlist + sampling rules for per-variant metrics; validate dashboards stay under cardinality budgets.
Complete audit log payload review and confirm no prompt/PII is included in diffs by default.
Run full staging E2E suite with streaming + retries + rollback drill; attach results to release checklist.

Marcus Lin + Kevin Osei: sign off audit event payload fields (before/after diffs, actor attribution) and confirm retention/export format by 2024-10-18.
Dylan Brooks + Chloe Martin: confirm Console error states for entitlement/RBAC denials and guardrail validation; implement final copy changes by 2024-10-17.
Mina Haddad: publish final stickiness default decision (optional vs default-on) and update routing semantics doc by 2024-10-17.
Leila Farouk: run GA preflight test pass in staging (including failure injection + rollback drill) and post report by 2024-10-18.

[00:00] Talia Benson: Alright, top of the hour. This is the GA readiness sync for Hosted canary rollouts. Goal today is basically: what’s still open, what’s actually done, and do we have any hidden dragons before we set a date for the flag flip.

[00:18] Marissa Cole: Yep. And just to anchor: we’re calling GA when the Console workflow is self-serve for eligible plans, with guardrails, audit trail, and we can actually support it on-call without tribal knowledge.

[00:32] Talia Benson: Great. I’m going to run through the checklist and ask each team for status. Connor, can you keep us honest on what’s a hard gate vs “nice to have”?

[00:41] Connor O’Brien: Yeah, I’ve got the release checklist open. There are like… twelve hard gates. The rest is polish.

[00:49] Talia Benson: Cool. First: control plane policy schema and propagation reliability.

[00:56] Ethan Park: Policy schema v2 is in, migration is in staging. The main remaining concern is the regional propagation staleness issue we saw last week. That was the case where us-east updated weights, eu-west stayed on the previous version for like a minute-ish.

[01:16] Jordan Lee: The fix is the monotonic version check and retry. It’s in review, and it removes the “last write wins but out of order” behavior. The edge case was during simultaneous edits—Console update, then auto-step, then someone hit pause.

[01:35] Sean Gallagher: From SRE side, that one’s a gate. Not because a minute is catastrophic for canary, but because it caused surprising behavior and support tickets in beta. If we GA and it happens again, it becomes a trust issue.

[01:50] Paula Mendes: What’s the confidence it’s fully addressed? Like do we have a repro test?

[01:55] Jordan Lee: We added an integration test that forces two updates with skewed timing and asserts every region converges to the highest version. It’s not perfect, but it hits the class of bug.

[02:08] Talia Benson: ETA to merge and deploy?

[02:11] Ethan Park: If no surprises, tomorrow for merge, then staging Thursday morning, prod early next week behind the flag.

[02:21] Connor O’Brien: For the train, I’d prefer it’s in prod at least 48 hours before we flip GA on. So we can watch it.

[02:30] Talia Benson: Noted. Next: routing integration—weighted splits and stickiness and streaming semantics.

[02:38] Mina Haddad: Weighted variants are live in Hosted data plane behind the canary flag. The main question is stickiness defaults. Right now it’s optional: you can enable request-hash stickiness per route. If you don’t, it’s random weighting.

[02:55] Marissa Cole: Product-wise we’ve been telling customers it’s “recommended” for evaluation stability, not required. But we should decide what happens in Console by default.

[03:05] Dylan Brooks: In the wizard, we default stickiness to on, with an info tooltip. But that’s based on an earlier conversation—if routing says we shouldn’t, we need to change it.

[03:17] Ravi Menon: (joined late) Sorry, one sec. Yeah, the tradeoff is fairness and cache. Stickiness can cause certain tenants to see more candidate if the hash is correlated with some header. Also, for streaming sessions, we already pin variant at start so there’s no cross mixing.

[03:36] Emily Zhao: Just to clarify, the streaming behavior: we select baseline or candidate at request start, and retries reuse the same selection. That part is in and tested. What’s tricky is if customers do their own client retries and the request id changes.

[03:52] Mina Haddad: Exactly. If they send a stable idempotency key or session id header, we can honor that; otherwise it’s a new request. The doc needs to be clear.

[04:03] Sean Gallagher: For GA, we need “rollback doesn’t break streaming”. Meaning: if you roll back mid-stream, the stream continues on the originally selected backend. We can’t suddenly switch model half way.

[04:15] Mina Haddad: That’s how it is today. Selection happens at the start and it stays pinned.

[04:20] Marcus Lin: From security, just make sure we’re not leaking anything in the stickiness hash key. If it’s derived from request headers, those sometimes contain emails or user ids.

[04:31] Mina Haddad: It’s a configurable key; we recommend a stable opaque user id, not raw PII. By default we use an internal request id hash, not customer’s raw headers.

[04:44] Dylan Brooks: Okay, so action for us is: decide default stickiness in UI and what warning text we show.

[04:51] Talia Benson: I’ll capture it. Next: telemetry and dashboards.

[04:57] Logan Wright: Per-variant tagging is in: we tag baseline/candidate variant and model version. The concern is cardinality explosion if we include route id and organization id together plus variant. We need the allowlist so we don’t end up with ten million series.

[05:17] Thomas Baird: (audio crackly) Uh, yeah, we want to cap high-card tags. Specifically route should be present, but we need aggregation at route group for some views. Otherwise a customer with thousands of routes… we die.

[05:29] Allison Grant: The dashboards we’re shipping show per-route compare for a selected route, not global across every route. For that, we can query filtered time series. But the backend still has to store it.

[05:42] Nadia Rahman: Also cost metrics. We’re tracking token cost deltas per variant. That can be heavy because it includes input tokens vs output tokens. We’re not including prompt text, just counts.

[05:55] Paula Mendes: What’s the plan to keep it stable? Sampling?

[05:59] Logan Wright: Two pieces. One: enforce tag allowlist: route_id, variant, model_version, region. No user id, no request id. Two: if an org exceeds a route limit, we aggregate to route_group for default panels and only allow per-route for top N routes.

[06:18] Sean Gallagher: That’s a gate. We need to be confident enabling this feature doesn’t cause our metrics bill to go nuts and also doesn’t degrade ingestion.

[06:28] Logan Wright: We can provide a back-of-the-envelope cardinality estimate today in Slack. Right now in staging it’s okay.

[06:36] Talia Benson: Please do. Also: do we have alerts? Allison?

[06:41] Allison Grant: Draft alerts are ready: baseline vs candidate error rate delta, p95 latency delta, and also “propagation staleness” for control plane. But we need to finalize thresholds and what’s paging vs ticket.

[06:56] Sean Gallagher: We should page if staleness > 60 seconds for more than 5 minutes, and ticket if it’s like 15 seconds sustained. For customer route-level canary deltas, we probably do not page on every customer canary, but we should have internal guardrails that can auto-pause a rollout if we see crazy 5xx.

[07:15] Marissa Cole: Auto-pause is in scope? I thought we only had “guardrails block progression / show warnings”.

[07:21] Jada Williams: We have policy evaluation that can mark a rollout as “violating” and prevent timed progression. But auto-pause is a separate action that changes routing weights. Today it’s manual.

[07:33] Sean Gallagher: Okay. Then minimum is: dashboards and clear runbook for “pause now, set candidate to 0%”.

[07:42] Rafael Mendes: Runbook is drafted. It includes commands to force a rollback and verify via the compare dashboard. But it needs links updated once dashboards are final.

[07:55] Talia Benson: We’ll link it up. Next: audit logging.

[08:00] Kevin Osei: The event types are create/update/pause/rollback. Payload includes actor, org, route, and before/after policy snapshot. The open question is the “diff formatting” and what we do about potential sensitive values.

[08:17] Marcus Lin: Yeah, we should assume route names and model aliases might contain sensitive strings. Not PII usually, but sometimes folks put customer names. We should avoid logging freeform notes fields. Also make sure we’re not logging raw headers or prompts.

[08:34] Chloe Martin: Console doesn’t send prompts or headers. It sends policy config and guardrail thresholds. Those are like numbers and model ids.

[08:42] Kevin Osei: Agreed. But the diff includes route id and route display name. We can keep the id, but maybe we should not log display name.

[08:51] Marissa Cole: Wouldn’t that make the audit trail less usable?

[08:54] Marcus Lin: We can log display name in the product UI but keep audit log export minimal. Or we can hash it. The compliance expectation is actor + action + what changed. Route id is enough if you can map it.

[09:10] Dylan Brooks: In the Console activity timeline we can show the nice names. That’s separate from the audit log export.

[09:17] Kevin Osei: Perfect. We’ll keep export payload lean: ids + policy version + before/after numeric fields + model identifiers.

[09:29] Talia Benson: Is security signoff dependent on that change?

[09:33] Marcus Lin: Yes. Not a blocker if it’s implemented this week.

[09:38] Connor O’Brien: Please treat it as a gate. If we ship audit logs, we should ship them right.

[09:44] Talia Benson: Noted. Next: Console workflow and guardrails.

[09:50] Dylan Brooks: Wizard is implemented. Create/edit, preview effective routing, activity timeline, pause and rollback flows. The biggest thing is validation copy and safe defaults. Right now we block 100% candidate if no guardrails are set.

[10:07] Paula Mendes: What’s “guardrails set” mean? Like all of them or at least one?

[10:10] Chloe Martin: At least one of: error rate threshold, latency threshold, or cost per token delta. Quality gate is optional and only for customers with the evals integration.

[10:23] Marissa Cole: I want to make sure this is consistent with pricing/entitlements. Like we can’t show quality gate toggles to folks who don’t have it.

[10:31] Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC/entitlements: we check on create/edit/pause/rollback. If you don’t have the plan, it returns a specific error code. Console shows “Contact sales / upgrade” message.

[10:45] Dylan Brooks: There’s one UX question: for users without permission, do we hide the button or show it disabled? We currently show disabled with tooltip.

[10:55] Marcus Lin: For security, disabling is okay as long as we don’t leak configuration details. But since it’s within the same org, it’s not super sensitive.

[11:05] Sean Gallagher: On-call: I’d rather it’s visible but blocked with a clear message so support can see why a customer is stuck.

[11:14] Talia Benson: Great. QA status.

[11:17] Leila Farouk: E2E tests are mostly green. We cover: create rollout baseline/candidate, step weights 1% -> 10% -> 50%, timed progression on/off, invalid percent sum, missing guardrails, pause, rollback, and delete route while rollout exists (expected error). We still need the streaming retry scenario in CI; right now it’s manual because the harness is flaky.

[11:44] Mina Haddad: The streaming test flakiness might be our side—long tail of cold start. We can increase timeouts.

[11:52] Leila Farouk: Yeah. Also we need failure injection: simulate one region being down and confirm routing fallback doesn’t violate canary semantics.

[12:02] Sean Gallagher: We don’t do cross-region fallback for Hosted within a single request today unless the customer has multi-region enabled, right?

[12:09] Mina Haddad: Correct. But even within a region, we might move between capacity pools. That shouldn’t change variant.

[12:16] Leila Farouk: Okay. We can scope it to “pause and rollback propagate to all regions within SLO”.

[12:26] Talia Benson: Docs readiness.

[12:29] Elliot Price: Docs are in final review. We have: how to create rollouts in Console, guardrails explanation, monitoring guidance, and troubleshooting. Biggest open is clarifying stickiness and streaming semantics. Also we need a “known caveats” section: metrics take a few minutes to show up, and timed steps require guardrails to be set.

[12:52] Marissa Cole: Also “migration from beta”. We should have a callout for customers already using the beta flags.

[12:58] Elliot Price: Yep, there’s a section. It says beta rollouts will be migrated and the UI will reflect the new schema. If something fails, contact support.

[13:07] Connor O’Brien: Release timing: We need to align docs publish with flag enable. Not a week earlier.

[13:13] Talia Benson: Okay. Let’s go to go/no-go. What are the blockers?

[13:18] Sean Gallagher: Blockers from SRE: (1) propagation fix in prod and observed stable, (2) SLOs and alerts wired, (3) runbook links correct, (4) at least one rollback drill executed end-to-end.

[13:35] Marcus Lin: Security blockers: audit event payload finalization and a quick review of RBAC mappings. Also confirm we’re not logging route display names or any customer-provided freeform strings in export.

[13:49] Logan Wright: Telemetry blocker: tag allowlist and cardinality guard. Without it I’m nervous.

[13:56] Dylan Brooks: Console blocker: copy tweaks and final permission states. Not huge.

[14:03] Marissa Cole: Product blocker: stickiness default decision. Also, we need to be clear on what we promise: this is Hosted only, not Dedicated, not Private, for this GA.

[14:13] Talia Benson: Connor, anything else on the checklist?

[14:16] Connor O’Brien: Also the staged rollout plan: which regions first, and the flag ramp. And sign-offs: Product, Console Eng, Platform Eng, Routing, SRE, Security, Docs. We need names attached.

[14:31] Talia Benson: Let’s talk staged plan. Proposal: enable GA flag for internal dogfood in prod first, then 5% of eligible orgs in us-east, then expand to remaining US regions, then EU.

[14:45] Sean Gallagher: Works. Don’t do EU first; our observability there is slightly less mature.

[14:51] Paula Mendes: How do we pick 5%? Random by org id hash?

[14:55] Connor O’Brien: Exactly, and we can override for named accounts.

[15:00] Marissa Cole: We should also hand-pick a few beta-friendly customers. Support is ready to watch them.

[15:08] Talia Benson: Yep. For internal, we’ll do the Redwood staging route and a few internal apps.

[15:15] Dylan Brooks: Also: we should ensure the “preview effective routing” endpoint is not slow. It hits policy evaluation.

[15:22] Ethan Park: It’s cached. But we should verify latency with load.

[15:28] Allison Grant: Our control plane SLO is p95 evaluation under 100ms, right?

[15:33] Ethan Park: That’s the target, but depends on whether you include storage reads. We can define it as in-memory evaluation excluding DB.

[15:43] Sean Gallagher: For customer experience it includes the full path. But preview is not on the request path for inference, it’s Console. Still, it should feel snappy.

[15:54] Talia Benson: Let’s not bikeshed the number here; Sean and Allison can propose thresholds and we’ll align.

[16:02] (crosstalk)

[16:03] Marissa Cole: Can we talk guardrail defaults? In the wizard, what thresholds do we prefill?

[16:09] Dylan Brooks: Current defaults: error rate delta 1% absolute, latency p95 delta 15%, cost per token delta 20%. Users can change.

[16:21] Paula Mendes: 1% absolute might be too strict for low traffic. It’ll false trigger.

[16:27] Sana Farid: Right, statistically it’s noisy. But we’re not auto-pausing. It’s just a guardrail. We should explain “insufficient data” and not block progression due to noise.

[16:39] Chloe Martin: The backend can treat it as “no verdict” until min sample size.

[16:45] Sean Gallagher: Please make sure the UI says that. Otherwise people will think we’re broken.

[16:50] Dylan Brooks: We have a copy line: “Guardrails evaluate when sufficient traffic is observed.” Might need to be more explicit.

[16:59] Elliot Price: We can add that to docs too.

[17:03] Talia Benson: Okay. Let’s fast forward—any other risks?

[17:07] Mina Haddad: One more: if someone edits weights repeatedly, we should ensure we don’t thrash caches. But for canary it’s expected. The data plane uses a configuration push every few seconds.

[17:20] Jordan Lee: Rate limit on policy updates helps. We have server-side throttling: no more than one update per 10 seconds per route.

[17:28] Dylan Brooks: In UI, we also debounce.

[17:31] Sean Gallagher: Perfect. Also, for incident response, do we have a “big red button”? Like force baseline now.

[17:39] Hannah Rivera: Rollback sets candidate to 0 and locks schedule. Pause freezes the current split. We have a separate “force baseline” action in the runbook that calls the rollback endpoint.

[17:52] Talia Benson: Great.

[17:54] Kevin Osei: On audit logs: we need to ensure pause/rollback events include who initiated and from where (API vs Console). We can add “actor_type” = user/service.

[18:06] Chloe Martin: That’s already there, I think. But I’ll double check.

[18:10] Marcus Lin: Also include request id for internal tracing. That’s not customer data.

[18:15] Chloe Martin: Yep, request id and correlation id are present.

[18:20] Talia Benson: Okay, I want to do a quick round: are we on track for GA next week?

[18:25] Sean Gallagher: If the propagation fix lands tomorrow and we get 48 hours in prod, yeah, maybe end of next week.

[18:33] Marcus Lin: Same. Assuming audit payload change lands.

[18:37] Logan Wright: Telemetry changes by tomorrow, I’m good.

[18:41] Leila Farouk: QA needs two full days for the regression pass once everything is merged.

[18:47] Connor O’Brien: So realistically: Friday is tight. Monday/Tuesday following week feels safer.

[18:54] Marissa Cole: I’d rather be safe. Customers care more that it works than the exact day.

[19:00] Talia Benson: Cool. Let’s align on a target: tentative GA flag to 5% us-east Tuesday, then ramp Thursday if no issues.

[19:11] Connor O’Brien: Works, with an explicit rollback criteria list.

[19:15] Allison Grant: Rollback criteria: sustained 5xx increase on control plane endpoints, propagation staleness > 60s, metrics ingestion issues, or customer canaries causing spikes? Though we can’t police customer configs.

[19:30] Sean Gallagher: Rollback criteria is for the platform feature itself: if enabling GA causes unexpected platform load or incidents. Customer misconfigs are handled via guardrails and support.

[19:41] Marissa Cole: But we should prevent the worst misconfig. Like “100% candidate with no guardrails” should be blocked, and also maybe require confirm for >50%.

[19:51] Dylan Brooks: We have a confirmation modal for >50% candidate and for removing all guardrails.

[19:58] Talia Benson: Great. I’m going to capture action items now.

[20:03] Talia Benson: Sean and Allison: finalize SLO thresholds and paging policy. Logan: post cardinality estimate and land allowlist. Marcus/Kevin: audit payload signoff. Mina: stickiness default decision. Leila: staging rollback drill. Elliot: docs final updates for stickiness/streaming.

[20:28] Talia Benson: Anything else before we end?

[20:31] Marissa Cole: Just one—support enablement. Dev Patel and Owen had questions about how to interpret “candidate worse than baseline” charts. We should do a quick 20-minute training.

[20:43] Sean Gallagher: We can do that after dashboards are final.

[20:47] Connor O’Brien: Add to checklist: internal comms in #releases and #support with the runbook link.

[20:54] Talia Benson: Done. Alright, I’ll send notes and update the release checklist. Thanks all.
